item.title: Hidden pain! Why did investors lose money in 750 smallcaps when Nifty rallied 2500 points?
item.description: The Nifty has rallied nearly 13% in a month, but the recovery has bypassed hundreds of smaller stocks. ACE Equity data shows 769 stocks declined between October 8 and November 8, with several well-known companies losing over 20%. Here’s why the market rebound remains narrow and which stocks have suffered the steepest losses.
item.dc:creator: Akash Podishetti
item.content:encoded: The Nifty has staged a strong recovery over the past month, surging nearly 13% as foreign investors returned to Dalal Street and heavyweight stocks bounced back from their recent lows. Yet, the rally has brought little relief to hundreds of smallcap investors, with more than 750 stocks delivering negative returns during the same period.An analysis of stock market data compiled by ACE Equity shows that 769 stocks declined between October 8 and November 8, even as the benchmark Nifty recovered sharply. The Nifty climbed 2,812 points, or 12.65%, during this period.The contrasting performance highlights the narrow nature of the market recovery, with foreign institutional investors (FIIs) largely favouring established large-cap companies, while smaller stocks continue to struggle. The weakness has been particularly painful for retail investors, many of whom have substantial exposure to midcap and smallcap companies following their strong performance in previous years.Hundreds of stocks remain under pressureSeveral well-known companies feature among the stocks that have declined despite the Nifty's recovery. According to ACE Equity data, eMudhra fell 33.73% between October 8 and November 8, while Wardwizard Innovations & Mobility declined 32.53%.Genesys International lost 31.58%, Morepen Laboratories dropped 30.93%, and KRN Heat Exchanger & Refrigeration fell 30.90%. Sterlite Technologies declined 30.22%, while MTAR Technologies slipped 26.79%. Electronics Mart India lost 24.39%, Kirloskar Oil Engines fell 24.54%, and RR Kabel declined 21.44%.Other notable laggards included Netweb Technologies, down 16.91%, HFCL, down 15.88%, and Praj Industries, which lost 12.29%.Also Read: FIIs are back with a bang but why are stocks from only 2 sectors their favourites? The losses show that the market recovery has left behind a substantial number of companies across technology, pharmaceuticals, engineering, manufacturing and other sectors.For investors holding these stocks, the sharp improvement in benchmark indices has done little to offset the damage suffered during the broader market correction.Why is Nifty rising while smallcaps struggle?Apurva Sheth, Head of Market Perspectives and Research at SAMCO Securities, believes the divergence comes down to buying being concentrated in a handful of heavyweight stocks. A lot of investors are scratching their heads thinking why their portfolio isn't moving up with Nifty. The simple answer is you don't own what is moving up, Sheth said.According to his analysis, the Nifty Top 10 Equal Weight Index gained 10.64% over the preceding month, while the Nifty Midcap 150 and Nifty Smallcap 250 indices each declined 2.74%. The Nifty Microcap 250 fell 5.32%.The first major reason behind the divergence is valuation. Several largecap stocks had suffered heavy losses during the market correction that began in January 2026, bringing their valuations to more attractive levels.This encouraged investors to return to established companies as crude oil prices eased and concerns about the global economic outlook moderated.Smaller companies, meanwhile, entered the correction with relatively elevated valuations following their earlier rallies. Investors have remained selective amid concerns about earnings visibility and the sustainability of growth.Foreign money is chasing large companiesThe second major factor is the return of foreign institutional investors. After months of sustained selling, overseas investors have begun deploying substantial capital into Indian equities, helping lift banking, technology, telecommunications and other heavyweight stocks.Foreign investors have bought more than $4.1 billion worth of Indian equities so far in November, according to Reuters, marking the strongest monthly inflow since September 2024. However, foreign institutions generally prefer large, liquid companies where they can deploy substantial amounts without significantly affecting share prices.This has benefited stocks such as ICICI Bank, HDFC Bank, Infosys, Bharti Airtel and Reliance Industries. According to Sheth, ICICI Bank and Infosys each gained 16% over his one-month review period, while Bharti Airtel advanced 14.61%. Kotak Mahindra Bank rose 10.08%, HDFC Bank gained 10%, and Reliance Industries climbed 8.44%.The ten heavyweight stocks in his analysis delivered an average return of 10.19%, highlighting how concentrated the rebound has been.For smaller companies, the absence of similar institutional buying has limited the recovery despite improving sentiment across the broader market.Can the broader market catch up?The broader market has also faced pressure from stretched valuations, uneven earnings performance and reduced risk appetite following months of geopolitical uncertainty and high crude oil prices.Although the September-quarter earnings season has shown signs of improvement, investors are increasingly distinguishing between companies delivering sustainable profit growth and those whose earlier valuations were driven by aggressive expectations.The next test for Dalal Street will be whether sustained foreign inflows and stronger corporate earnings encourage buying beyond the largest companies.Disclosure: This article was written by Podishetti Akash, who is not a SEBI-registered Research Analyst or an Investment Adviser. Podishetti Akash and his ‘relative(s)’ (as defined under Section 2(77) of the Companies Act, 2013) do not hold any financial interest in the companies mentioned in this article as of the date of publication. The views/recommendations mentioned in this article, wherever applicable, are those of the respective SEBI-registered Research Analyst/brokerage and have been reproduced/reported with due attribution. They should not be construed as the views or recommendations of The Economic Times Digital or the journalist. Readers are advised to consider the original research report and make their investment decisions based on their own assessment. Brokerage disclosures here.

item.title: Chinese commentators see a political plot behind the Jensen Huang extramarital affair scandal
item.description: Chinese commentators suggest that Jensen Huang’s advocacy for continued access to the Chinese market, and his criticism of US chip restrictions may have made him a target of greater scrutiny.
item.dc:creator: Sana Hashmi
item.content:encoded:
-->

Eye On China

Chinese commentators see a political plot behind the Jensen Huang extramarital affair scandal

Chinese commentators suggest that Jensen Huang’s advocacy for continued access to the Chinese market, and his criticism of US chip restrictions may have made him a target of greater scrutiny.

Sana Hashmi

11 November, 2026 08:30 am IST

Follow Us:

-->

Facebook

X

LinkedIn

WhatsApp

Email

Copy Link

A photo shows NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang with a woman confirmed by a Reuters source to be Alice Huang in Taipei, Taiwan released on June 7, 2024. Obtained by Reuters/via REUTERS

Stay updated with ThePrint:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

-->

A headline on the Chinese news website Guancha declared that “The hunt for Nvidia is beginning to close in.” It captures a growing narrative in Chinese commentary that the controversy over Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s extramarital affair with Alice Huang is being used by Washington and Wall Street to increase pressure on the chipmaker.

A viral Weibo post highlighted Alice Huang’s career at Chinese state broadcasters Hunan TV and CCTV News , HSBC Private Bank and CITIC Securities, before she became managing director of Singapore-based Megaspeed in 2023. Claims that she had links to China and used her relationship with Huang to obtain chip-related information and circumvent export controls have been dismissed on Chinese internet as unsubstantiated .

The affair sparked intense debate across the Chinese internet since 30 October , before Jensen Huang’s public apology to his wife, in which he confessed to cheating. Discussion has ranged from national security and Huang’s private life to Nvidia’s future. On Weibo, there are hashtags about Huang admitting to infidelity, along with views that his confession was addressed to Capitol Hill.

Show Full Article

Beyond Huang’s private life For most Chinese commentators, the controversy has moved well beyond Huang’s personal reputation. Jin Yan , a special contributor to Caijing Magazine , argued that Huang’s personal relationships now raise questions about national security, export controls, and the consequences could extend across the entire AI supply chain.

A Baijiahao commentary makes a similar distinction: the focus, it argues, is on reports of foreign intelligence targeting Huang, rather than his infidelity.

Others have focused on what the scandal reveals about Nvidia itself. A Weibo post argued that while Huang’s infidelity is a personal moral issue, it also exposes the company’s dependence on its founder. After three decades under his leadership, Nvidia has no publicly announced succession plan, with little indication that Huang intends to step down. The post suggests that Huang’s growing geopolitical exposure could prompt investors to reassess key-person risk and its implications for the company’s valuation.

Shen Yi, a professor of international politics at Fudan University, placed the controversy surrounding Huang within the broader United States-China technology competition. He argued that Nvidia faces a security challenge shaped by competing approaches in Washington. Democrats may seek to curb AI expansion through regulation, while Republicans focus on national security and technology controls. Although their methods differ, both approaches could constrain American technology companies.

This, according to Shen, exposes a broader contradiction in US policy: Washington wants to maintain American dominance in AI while restricting China’s access to advanced computing, even as US companies and investors have strong commercial incentives to pursue opportunities in the Chinese market.

Espionage claims and the China factor In Chinese commentary, the espionage allegations are viewed largely through the lens of US-China rivalry. Some see them as another way for Washington to put pressure on a US technology company with deep commercial interests in China.

One analysis argued that American media have distorted the story to promote a broader anti-China narrative. It points to the portrayal of Huang’s association with an Asian woman as a potential intelligence link, and his calls for easing chip restrictions as evidence of Chinese influence.

The author suggests that Huang’s ‘Chinese’ heritage and position on the Chinese market have made him a target of US hawks. The allegations, the analysis argued, are intended to pressure Silicon Valley, stoke security fears and undermine prospects for improved US-China relations.

Other Chinese commentators focus on what the allegations could mean for Nvidia, regardless of whether espionage is established. Chinese publication World Science Pioneer said that media reports linking the controversy to foreign intelligence and national security risks have attracted much of the attention. Even if an investigation finds no leakage of trade secrets, the episode could still lead US regulators, customers and business partners to impose stricter requirements on information security, conflict-of-interest reviews and external communications.

A commentator pointed to bipartisan agreement in Washington on preventing advanced computing power from secretly reaching China.

Another Baijiahao commentary sees the scrutiny of Nvidia as following a familiar US political playbook: first accusations of chip transshipment, now allegations of intelligence links.

“The goals may change, but the script remains the same,” it said, drawing parallels with the earlier targeting of Huawei.

The author argued that as China narrows the US technological lead in AI, Washington is increasingly using political pressure to obstruct its rival, reflecting anxiety about its own technological competitiveness.

The message to Nvidia, it concludes, is clear: “If you obediently follow orders and cut off ties with China, then we’ll let you off the hook.”

Why now? The politics behind the timing For some Chinese commentators, the timing of the espionage controversy is important. They see it against the backdrop of Washington’s shifting approach to semiconductor exports and the continuing struggle over China’s access to advanced chips.

One commentary argued that Nvidia is caught between selective easing of chip export restrictions to China and continued scrutiny of its compliance with export controls. Huang has repeatedly criticised US restrictions, arguing that they undermine American competitiveness and push China to accelerate its own technological development.

Huang’s public support for open-weight AI models, including Chinese models, has also put him at odds with Washington’s more hawkish approach. Against this backdrop, the Chinese commentator questions why the allegations have surfaced now, suggesting they reflect wider geopolitical tensions over Nvidia’s continued business ties with China.

Another comment takes the argument further. It suggests that linking Huang’s personal scandal to allegations of Chinese espionage serves several political objectives: weakening his influence in Washington, discouraging Silicon Valley executives from advocating a softer approach toward China, providing justification for tighter chip export controls, and reinforcing the China threat narrative ahead of a new Congress.

Not all the commentary sees the controversy as an attempt to damage Nvidia itself.

A Weibo post said that new Democrat lawmakers could use the affair to warn other major technology companies that corporate misconduct carries consequences, without necessarily seeking to undermine Nvidia.

Writing for Guancha , Li Limeng offered a broader interpretation, presenting the controversy as part of a struggle for control of the US AI industry. In this account, Democrat establishment elites are seeking to consolidate their influence over AI models, energy infrastructure and semiconductor production through political networks, corporate appointments and governance mechanisms.

Also read: India is not an ally on demand. Its foreign policy must answer to its own people

A personal scandal with wider consequences Chinese reactions to the affair are far from uniform. They range from concerns about corporate governance and national security to claims of political manoeuvring in Washington. Yet a recurring theme is that the controversy cannot be separated from the wider US-China technology rivalry.

Some commentators suggest that Huang’s advocacy for continued access to the Chinese market, and his criticism of US chip restrictions, may have made him a target of greater scrutiny. They suspect that Huang’s personal relationships are now being used against him and viewed through the lens of national security.

Some see the affair as a means of putting pressure on Huang and Nvidia, while narrowing the space for US-China technology cooperation. Others believe its consequences could extend beyond the company, affecting the rules governing technology leaders and the direction of the global AI industry. In this reading, what began as a personal scandal involving one of the world’s most prominent technology executives has become part of a much larger debate about the future of AI and the intensifying US-China rivalry.

Sana Hashmi, PhD, is a fellow at the Taiwan-Asia Exchange Foundation and George HW Bush Foundation for US-China Relations. She tweets @sanahashmi1. Views are personal.

(Edited by Ratan Priya)

item.title: Thune, Jordan emerge as Republican minority leaders for next US Congress
item.description: The Republicans will be the minority party in both chambers of Congress during the final two years of Trump's presidency.
item.dc:creator: CNA

Thune, Jordan emerge as Republican minority leaders for next US Congress

The Republicans will be the minority party in both chambers of Congress during the final two years of Trump's presidency.

US Representative Jim Jordan (R-Ohio) speaks during a US House Judiciary subcommittee hearing on sanctuary city policies, on Capitol Hill in Washington, DC on Jun 30, 2026. (File photo: Reuters/Aaron Schwartz)

11 Nov 2026 10:13AM (Updated: 11 Nov 2026 10:15AM)

FAST

WASHINGTON: Republicans chose US Senate Majority Leader John Thune and House Judiciary Committee Chairman Jim Jordan on Tuesday (Nov 10) to lead them against a Democratic-controlled Congress that will take power in January for the final two years of Donald Trump's presidency. A week after Republicans lost their majority in a stinging midterm election defeat, Senate Republicans chose Thune by acclamation at a closed-door meeting for the task of trying to thwart Democratic initiatives that do not meet with their approval, including by wielding the Senate filibuster. "We're not going to be running this place next year," Thune told reporters. "But you can be assured we will be very, very active in asserting conservative priorities in all of the legislating ... that goes on here." Jordan's election as House minority leader elevates a combative Trump ally to the forefront of the party’s fight to defend the US president’s agenda in the lower chamber. Jordan defeated House Majority Leader Steve Scalise in a secret ballot. House Speaker Mike Johnson opted not to stand for the leadership position.

US Senate Majority Leader John Thune (R-South Dakota) speaks at a press conference on the day of the Senate Republican caucus leadership elections at the US Capitol in Washington, DC, on Nov 10, 2026. (File photo: Reuters/Elizabeth Frantz)

The House and Senate leadership elections will help to determine what role Republicans intend to play as the minority party in Congress during the final two years of Trump's presidency. Democrats will need Republican support to move major initiatives in the 100-member Senate, where the filibuster rule requires 60 votes for most legislation. Their majorities in both chambers also fall well short of the two-thirds of votes needed to override presidential vetoes. Thune, 65, a South Dakota Republican known for his consensus-building leadership style, is respected by Republicans and Democrats alike. But he has run afoul of Trump's MAGA supporters who say he did not move aggressively enough to enact Trump's policies on immigration and election reform. After the midterm elections, Thune vowed that Republicans would work with Trump to block "Democrat extremism" and work against any attempt by Democrats to unwind Republican achievements, including border security and judicial appointments. Jordan, 62, was first elected in 2006 to represent a deeply conservative rural district in northern Ohio and was a founder of the House Freedom Caucus, a group that former Republican House Speaker John Boehner labelled "legislative terrorists". Before entering politics, Jordan honed his pugilistic style during a career as a high school and university champion wrestler, and later as a wrestling coach at Ohio State University. That past threatened his political career in 2018 when former students accused him of turning a blind eye to rampant sexual abuse of college wrestlers by the wrestling team's doctor, when Jordan was an assistant coach. Jordan denied all allegations, and a university investigation found no hard evidence that he knew of the abuse. But former wrestlers said the doctor's abuse was well-known and the report itself found that students had complained about the doctor's voyeurism in front of coaching staff. Jordan has often referred to his wrestling background in terms of his reputation as a fighter in Congress. He is known for his aggressive style of questioning in committee hearings. "I look at it like a wrestling match," Jordan told the New York Times in an April 2023 interview, explaining how he prepares for hearings. "I'm going to try to get as ready as I can. You can't just wing it."

item.title: Bulls in action! Sensex zooms 1,400 pts intraday; oil, FII buying aid rally
item.description: Experts said that strong FII participation in the past few sessions and better-than-expected corporate earnings are supporting the market rally.
item.content:encoded:
Home / Markets / News / Bulls in action! Sensex zooms 1,400 pts intraday; oil, FII buying aid rally

Bulls in action! Sensex zooms 1,400 pts intraday; oil, FII buying aid rally Experts said that strong FII participation in the past few sessions and better-than-expected corporate earnings are supporting the market rally.

Bulls in action! Sensex zooms 1,400 pts intraday; oil, FII buying aid rally

Abhinav Ranjan New Delhi 3 min read Last Updated : Nov 11 2026 | 3:40 PM IST

Listen to This Article

Stock market today, Sensex today: Market benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty 50 opened higher on Wednesday amid a correction in crude oil prices and heavy buying in financial stocks. Improving FII participation also supported the market sentiment.   The BSE Sensex made an intraday high of 82,520, up 1,411 points, or 1.74 per cent. Similarly, the 50-share Nifty benchmark touched a high of 25,424, up 380 points, or 1.52 per cent.   Experts said that strong FII participation in the past few sessions and better-than-expected corporate earnings are supporting the market rally. VK Vijayakumar, chief investment strategist, Geojit Investments, said that the sharp drop in crude oil prices is a relief for India.

"This surge was triggered mainly by aggressive FII buying. The dramatic change in the market environment was triggered by positive global cues for India from the weakening of the AI trade," he said.   The BSE Sensex closed 772.75 points, or 0.95 per cent higher at 81,879.40, while the Nifty 50 added 210.40 points, or 0.84 per cent, to settle at 25,255.05.   Also Read

Stock Market Close: Sensex pares gains but ends 773 pts up, Nifty at 25,255; PSU Bank rises 3%

Rentomojo climbs 10% to 52-wk high; what's behind gains as Q2 PAT dips 63%?

BHEL shares up 3.5% on Power Grid order for Gujarat synchronous condensers

Punjab National Bank share price soars 11% in two days; hits 52-week high

Bank Nifty tops 61,000, nears all-time high; what do charts say?

Check - TOP GAINERS NSE | TOP LOSERS NSE     Stock market today, Sensex today rally: Key reasons    Oil prices fall: Oil prices fell to two-month lows in the previous session, as the market swung between hopes for a de-escalation in the US-Iran war. At the last check, Brent futures climbed 0.78 per cent to $92.20 a barrel. US WTI crude traded at $86.53.

"The drop in Brent crude to $92 is an additional macro relief for India," VK Vijayakumar said.   Easing geopolitical tensions: US President Donald Trump has downplayed the need for additional military action against Iran "at this point," easing fears of sustained supply disruptions from the West Asia. However, Trump, in a Reuters interview and a later appearance in the White House press briefing room, said he plans to keep up a naval blockade in the Strait of Hormuz for now.   FPI inflows: VK Vijayakumar said that FPIs have turned aggressive buyers in the Indian stock market. In the past eight trading days, they pumped in over ₹55,000 crore into equities, the highest net inflows in the past six years.

"Given the new favourable environment for the Indian market, FIIs are likely to continue buying, imparting resilience to the frontline stocks in banking/financials, telecom, capital goods, select auto and pharmaceutical majors. This rally, which has more steam left, will be led again by large-caps," he said.   Banking & financial services shine: Today's rally was led by heavy buying in banking, and financial services stocks. At the close, the Nifty Bank index was up 1.76 per cent, with 13 of 14 constituents ending in the green. The Nifty Financial Services gained  1.02 per cent, with 17 out of 20 stocks finishing in the positive territory.

Strong earnings: VK Vijayakumar said that it is important to note that the real fundamental support to the rally has come from the better-than-expected Q2 results. The near 24 per cent earnings growth in Nifty 50 in Q2 is a 12 quarter high and has compressed the forward PE for Nifty 50 to fair levels.   Disclaimer: Views and outlook in this report belong to the brokerages and analysts cited. They do not reflect the views of Business Standard. Readers are advised to exercise discretion.

E20 row: Karnataka or OMCs, whom to believe? Auto execs call for independent ethanol content tests

Former executive director of Ford India Vinay Piparsania says petrol with over 20% ethanol would be of a different specification, needing regulatory approval and fresh assessments.

Udit Bubna

11 November, 2026 07:00 am IST

Follow Us:

New Delhi: Conflicting claims made by the Karnataka government and oil marketing companies (OMCs) over ethanol content in petrol have exposed the need for an independent mechanism to verify fuel quality, Vinay Piparsania, former executive director at Ford India and founder of MillenStrat Advisory & Research, an automotive consultancy firm, told ThePrint.

He said petrol containing more than the prescribed 20 percent ethanol cannot be sold as an E20 blend, and any move towards higher alcohol percentage would require a separate fuel specification, vehicle compatibility assessments and advance notification to consumers.

The controversy emerged after the Karnataka government alleged that petrol samples collected from retail outlets in the state contained ethanol concentrations of between 26 and 31 percent . The OMCs, however, disputed the findings and maintained that the fuel supplied through their networks met the prescribed specifications. The Kerala government has also sent petrol samples for testing.

Show Full Article

Piparsania said Karnataka’s concern was legitimate if petrol sold as E20 was found to contain 26–31 percent ethanol. Such a deviation would constitute a serious fuel-quality violation and a consumer-protection issue.

The OMCs have presented their own dataset comprising 893 samples tested across 27 states and Union Territories, including 56 samples from Karnataka. According to the companies, all these samples were within the prescribed 19–21 percent range.

“The OMC response is technically substantive and cannot be dismissed,” Piparsania said. However, he pointed out that these results largely came from the companies’ own quality-control systems and could not serve as the final independent assessment. He said the OMCs had also raised questions about Karnataka’s sampling procedures and the analytical methods used in the third-party test certificates.

“The OMCs have raised credible technical questions about the Karnataka testing, but the OMC’s own testing cannot by itself be the final referee. The dispute should be resolved through jointly collected samples and independent testing to the same prescribed standard. That is how you protect both consumer confidence, and the credibility of India’s ethanol programme,” he said.

Also Read: Karnataka alleges excess ethanol in E20 petrol, oil firms question testing methodology

Independent testing and OMC accountability Piparsania suggested a joint sampling exercise, involving the state government, OMCs and an independent regulator or observer. Samples should be sealed, counterpart samples preserved, and their movement documented through a clear chain of custody.

Testing should be conducted at an independent laboratory accredited by the National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories (NABL), using prescribed methods under the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) IS 17021 specifications. Complete results, including details of individual retail outlets, should also be made public, he said.

He said the controversy was less about whether ethanol content could be measured accurately and more about the independence and transparency of the testing process. Laboratory testing is technically reliable when sampling procedures, calibration and methodology are properly controlled. Simple field checks, including density measurements and water-extraction tests, can identify major deviations but should not replace prescribed laboratory testing.

A former senior executive of a major automobile manufacturer, speaking to ThePrint on condition of anonymity, said the controversy also pointed to shortcomings in the OMCs’ quality-control management. He said oil companies needed to be more transparent about their quality-control procedures, including whether ethanol blending takes place at refineries, depots or retail outlets, and what checks are carried out at each stage.

He added that OMCs are responsible for ensuring fuel quality, they need to strengthen monitoring and make their quality-control measures more transparent to consumers.

On the possible side-effects of the higher blend fuels, the executive said “OEMs have not yet tested the E30 fuel, so the side-effects are not yet known, but fuel efficiency will definitely drop.”

Higher blending raises vehicle compatibility concerns Beyond the immediate dispute, Piparsania said any move towards E25 or E30 could have implications for vehicles currently designed and certified for E20 or lower ethanol blends.

E20 is a defined fuel specification under IS 17021, not merely a government target for ethanol blending. Moving beyond it would effectively introduce a different fuel specification.

He explained that higher ethanol concentrations could affect fuel efficiency, engine performance and the durability of vehicle components.

Ethanol has lower energy content per litre than petrol, meaning higher blends could increase fuel consumption. They also require a richer air-fuel mixture, which could affect cold starts, drivability and combustion if vehicles have not been calibrated for them.

Higher concentrations could also raise durability concerns involving fuel pumps, injectors, seals, hoses and other fuel-system components.

However, Piparsania cautioned against assuming that every E20-compatible vehicle would immediately suffer damage if exposed to E25 or E30. “That does not mean an E25 or E30 blend will suddenly damage every E20 vehicle. But E20 certification is not E30 certification,” he said.

India’s existing vehicle fleet includes cars, two-wheelers and three-wheelers designed for different fuel specifications, ranging from E10 to E20. An older E10 vehicle cannot automatically be assumed to be compatible with higher blends. Similarly, E20 certification does not establish compatibility with E25 or E30.

Piparsania said automakers have not yet tested vehicles with ethanol blends beyond E20, making it difficult to assess the potential impact on vehicle components and long-term performance. However, higher ethanol concentrations are likely to reduce fuel efficiency, he said.

Piparsania said the government would need a vehicle-compatibility roadmap that considers vehicle categories, age and fuel-system technology.

He said the government had reportedly tasked the Automotive Research Association of India (ARAI) with evaluating E25 compatibility in existing E10- and E20-compatible vehicles, including long-duration testing of around 60,000–70,000 km. The findings should be available before any wider move towards E25, he added.

Higher blends would also require validation covering fuel-system durability, material compatibility, corrosion, engine starting, emissions, fuel economy and drivability.

Also Read: Centre questions Karnataka’s Ethanol testing process. So what is the prescribed procedure

Consumers need advance notice Piparsania said any decision to move beyond E20 must be accompanied by advance public notification, a defined transition period and adequate time for automakers to validate their vehicles.

Other safeguards should include mandatory labelling of fuel grades at petrol pumps, clear manufacturer warranty positions for different ethanol blends, and continued availability of compatible lower blends for older vehicles during the transition.

The government should also establish a mechanism for consumers to report complaints and seek compensation if fuel is found to be off-specification.

“Consumers should not have to determine, at their own cost, whether the fuel they purchased was within specification,” he said.

He said the dispute should be resolved through independent testing against the same prescribed standards to protect consumer confidence as well as the credibility of India’s ethanol-blending programme.

(Edited by Nardeep Singh Dahiya)

By Joshua McElwee BUENOS AIRES, Argentina, Nov 10 (Reuters) – Pope Leo drew a crowd of a million on Tuesday for the third strong turnout of his 12-day South America tour, as he urged young people at a nighttime vigil in Argentina not to be consumed by the pursuit of money or social media popularity.

Throngs stretched for miles down the Avenida del Libertador, one of Buenos Aires’ main boulevards. Many waved cell phones, screens shining in the black night, as Leo was driven slowly through the crowd in an open-air popemobile.

Chants of “This is the pope’s youth!” rang out as the vehicle stopped frequently so security officials could bring forward babies for Leo to bless.

Show Full Article

In a speech, the pope warned young people against worship of modern-day “idols” such as success or physical appearance, and lamented that some youth “go so far as to lie, betray or humiliate someone on social media.”

“Do not bow down before anything that cannot give you life,” he said.

Leo, on an ambitious three-country tour through November 17, led the vigil after returning from a day trip to Cordoba, Argentina’s second city, where he drew 650,000 people to an outdoor Mass earlier on Tuesday.

The pope led a Mass on Monday at the Avenida del Libertador that drew 2.5 million people, in the largest event of his 18-month-old papacy.

POPE SEEKS TO SHORE UP CATHOLIC STRONGHOLD

Leo is the first pope to visit Catholic-majority Argentina since 1987.

The pope, who is also visiting Uruguay and Peru on the tour, is seeking to reinforce a region that has long been a Catholic stronghold but where the Church has been losing ground to fast-growing evangelical denominations.

Leo has emerged as a forceful voice on the world stage, lamenting what he sees as a failure of global leadership. In Argentina, he has directly challenged President Javier Milei, a libertarian and close ally of US President Donald Trump.

On Sunday, Leo urged Milei, who has pushed an austerity agenda that the Church has criticized for cutting social services, not to target Argentina’s poorest. Milei has said spending cuts were necessary to bring inflation under control.

Valentin Gomez, 21, a student attending the Mass in Cordoba, praised Leo’s focus on those in need.

“In these difficult times we are living through, he is greatly needed,” Gomez said. “Someone who is truly concerned about the poor.”

Cordoba Cardinal Angel Sixto Rossi, a critic of the austerity policies, welcomed Leo’s visit as a chance for the pope to see how Argentina is suffering under Milei’s measures.

“He knows how beautiful our people are and the ugly part, the leadership of the government,” he said in an interview with Argentine media. “He doesn’t arrive blindfolded.”

Argentine Foreign Minister Pablo Quirno said Cordoba was chosen as a stop on the pope’s tour because of its location in the center of Argentina, allowing pilgrims to travel easily from neighboring provinces.

Leo, the first US-born pope, spent decades as a missionary in Peru. The Vatican has described the trip, one of the most demanding foreign tours by a pope in decades, as a “homecoming” for him.

(Reporting by Joshua McElwee, additional reporting by Leila Miller, Lucila Sigal, Horacio Soria; editing by Chizu Nomiyama, Rod Nickel and Stephen Coates)

US Treasury chief Bessent moved to military base after Iranian threats, NYT reports

WASHINGTON, Nov 10 (Reuters) – US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent recently moved out of his home and onto a military base after Iranian threats against his life, the New York Times reported on Tuesday, citing sources with knowledge of the matter.

Iran has ramped up efforts to target US personnel, and lethal plots by Tehran against American citizens have reached “advanced stages”, a senior intelligence official in the Trump administration warned in a memo seen by Reuters late last month.

The newspaper reported that the severity of the threats to Bessent was not immediately clear.

Show Full Article

Iran has previously denied plotting to attack officials and people on US soil.

The newspaper reported that US officials have noted that Iran’s ability to carry out large-scale attacks in the US and other territories overseas is limited.

The US Treasury Department did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Bessent has been the face of Washington’s economic pressure campaign against Tehran during the course of the US-Israeli war on Iran that began on February 28.

US-Israeli strikes on Iran and Israeli attacks on Lebanon during the war have killed thousands and displaced millions.

American and Israeli attacks have also killed top Iranian officials, including late Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.

(Reporting by Kanishka Singh in Washington; editing by Michelle Nichols )

item.title: All about Alice Huang, the Chinese banker linked to Nvidia's Jensen Huang
item.description: She was building a career in Chinese finance before turning to tech with a leadership role at a data centre company in Singapore. He is the high-profile CEO of Nvidia, the California-based company ...
item.content:encoded:
Home / World News / All about Alice Huang, the Chinese banker linked to Nvidia's Jensen Huang

All about Alice Huang, the Chinese banker linked to Nvidia's Jensen Huang Reports linking Huang to Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, who was accused of having ties to Beijing's intelligence service, have put Nvidia's chip exports and Megaspeed under scrutiny

Alice Huang (right) attending a dinner with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang at a restaurant in Taiwan in May 2025 | Photo: Reuters

AP Washington 5 min read Last Updated : Nov 11 2026 | 2:34 PM IST

Listen to This Article

She was building a career in Chinese finance before turning to tech with a leadership role at a data centre company in Singapore. He is the high-profile CEO of Nvidia, the California-based company that makes computer chips relied upon by advanced artificial intelligence systems. An affair between Nvidia's Jensen Huang and Alice Huang, who reportedly was suspected of working as a spy for Beijing, has rocked the tech and political worlds. The Chinese businesswoman also known as Huang Le had a close relationship with Jensen Huang, according to reports over the past month by the New York Times. The newspaper also reported that top policymakers were informed in a memo that intelligence indicated she was a spy for China's Ministry of State Security, recruited to influence Nvidia to make its most advanced chips more available in China.

In one widely shared photograph of the pair, Jensen Huang and people surrounding him are holding drinks in Taipei, while Alice Huang sits behind him, apparently watching him in conversation. The picture was posted in 2024 by software company NetThunder to its LinkedIn page. Also Read

Why Nvidia dominates AI, and what Huang's scandal could cost the firm

Nvidia has no clear successor to Jensen Huang. Who could take over?

China, Asean advance South China Sea pact talks, push deal to next year

Microsoft presses Trump admin to scuttle ban on Chinese data center tech

Jensen Huang's close ties to Trump come under scrutiny after spy claim

It remains unclear how long the affair lasted, and when exactly the relationship might have ended. The Associated Press was unable to reach Alice Huang for comment. Who is Alice Huang? Publicly available information about Alice Huang is scant. She was a Chinese finance executive before becoming involved in artificial intelligence, data centres and computer chips. In 2023, she became a director at Singapore-based Megaspeed, which describes itself as an "NVIDIA cloud partner". Last year, Megaspeed faced scrutiny from the US over its alleged skirting of US export restrictions and routing of a large amount of advanced Nvidia chips for Chinese users.

Megaspeed was incorporated in 2015 in Singapore with the name 7Road International, after being spun off as the overseas arm of a Chinese video game developer, according to corporate registration records. Filings show that in March 2023, it renamed itself Megaspeed International, with all of the shares transferred to Huang Le Limited, a company registered in the British Virgin Islands. That same month, Alice Huang became Megaspeed's controlling shareholder, according to research by the C4ADS, a Washington-based nonprofit focused on global security. But by November 2023, she was no longer listed as a director at Megaspeed, and all her shares were transferred to a Singaporean businessman, Tan Yong Pong, who also is known as James Tan.

While public records suggest Alice Huang left Megaspeed, short seller Culper Research issued a report in May this year that cited a Megaspeed employee saying Huang was "actually still our boss" and was still involved in the company's daily operations. Before Megaspeed, Alice Huang previously held senior positions at the Chinese firm Shanghai Hexi Investment Co. from around 2015 to 2017, according to social media posts and records from Simuwang, a Chinese private equity database. Her roles at Hexi included deputy general manager, executive director and member of the investment committee, according to Hexi's social media posts, among possible other roles. Hexi's founder Kang Wei, who appeared on some records alongside Alice Huang, was fined in 2018 by China's securities regulator 400,000 yuan (USD 60,000) over financial misconduct behaviours while Hexi was fined 17.7 million yuan (USD 2.7 million).

Before that, Alice Huang worked at HSBC's Hong Kong private banking arm and at CITIC Securities, a Chinese investment bank. HSBC and CITIC did not immediately respond to a request for comment on her employment history. Beijing has refuted claims that Alice Huang was a Chinese spy. Its Foreign Ministry said this week that the "Chinese spy allegation is unsubstantiated. It is nothing but smears against China". Why Megaspeed is at the centre of the controversy With the emergence of the latest scandal, Singapore-based AI computing company Megaspeed, where Alice Huang was a senior executive, is once again under the spotlight. Megaspeed, an Nvidia customer, was originally incorporated in 2015 before changing its name to Megaspeed International in 2023. Nvidia lists Megaspeed as a partner on its website, while Megaspeed says on its website it's "a core business partner of NVIDIA's computing power cloud business in the Asia-Pacific region".

It was the overseas gaming arm of Shenzhen-based developer 7Road Holdings Ltd. Late last year, Megaspeed denied accusations following reports that it was routing Nvidia chips to China, saying in a statement on its website that "there has been no evidence of any violations concerning the illicit transfer of chips or any illegal activities". Singapore's government said in late October, after fresh reports that Alice Huang was accused of being a Chinese intelligence source, that authorities were investigating Megaspeed and that Singapore "does not condone businesses" circumventing or violating other countries' export controls. However, it said, there were no investigations conducted in respect to Alice Huang.

Megaspeed did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

item.title: US House blocks bid to impeach Defense Secretary Hegseth
item.description: WASHINGTON: Republicans in the US House of Representatives blocked an effort on Tuesday (Nov 10) to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, winning a reprieve for the polarising Pentagon chief before Democrats take control of Congress next year and possibly try again.

US House blocks bid to impeach Defense Secretary Hegseth

US Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth holds a press briefing at the Pentagon in Washington, DC, US, Nov 10, 2026. (Photo: REUTERS/Evelyn Hockstein)

FAST

WASHINGTON: Republicans in the US House of Representatives blocked an effort on Tuesday (Nov 10) to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, winning a reprieve for the polarising Pentagon chief before Democrats take control of Congress next year and possibly try again. The vote on a procedural motion came just hours after Hegseth blasted efforts to impeach him as a farce and delivered a defiant defence of his record at the helm of the US military, winning praise from President Donald Trump. The chamber voted 211 to 204 in favour of a motion to refer eight articles of impeachment to the Republican-led House Judiciary Committee, a move that the sponsor of the impeachment push, US Representative Thomas Massie, warned would kill it. Massie, an outgoing Kentucky Republican, had hoped to draw votes from Republicans upset with Hegseth's policies and wary of the unpopularity of the eight-month-old Iran war but no other Republicans joined him. The US-Israeli led conflict has never been approved by Congress, which is the only branch of government constitutionally permitted to declare war.

Democrats had voiced strong support for the impeachment articles, which accuse Hegseth of the "high crimes and misdemeanours" of illegally ordering the military to wage war in Iran and Yemen, attack boats in the Caribbean Sea and capture Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro in January. But 11 Democrats, including former House Speaker Nancy Pelosi of California, did not vote. If eight of them had, the procedural measure would have been defeated, paving the way for a full House impeachment vote. Ian Krager, a spokesperson for Pelosi, said she had missed the vote because she had returned to San Francisco for an annual event to honour veterans, but would have voted against the procedural measure. Trump cheered the results in a social media post, saying the effort to impeach Hegseth "has miserably FAILED!" He wrote that Hegseth's performance on Iran, Venezuela and other issues "led to the EXONERATION of a Great American Patriot." Hegseth would have been the first US defence secretary to be impeached. The last time any civilian leader of the US military was impeached was in 1876, when William Belknap held the title "secretary of war". Hegseth calls himself secretary of war, part of his effort to rebrand a military he said was too weak and "woke" when he took office last year. Trump cannot change the name of the Defense Department without approval from Congress.

Related:

Trump vows comeback as bitter showdown with Congress looms

Trump revives election fraud claims after crushing midterm defeat

IRAN WAR ANGER Voter anger over the Iran war, which has settled into an effective stalemate focused on securing the Strait of Hormuz, helped Democrats win control of Congress in last week's midterm elections. A Reuters/Ipsos poll published on Tuesday found a majority of Americans want the newly elected Democratic-majority US Congress, which takes office in January, to act to end the war with Iran once and for all. Although Vice President JD Vance has publicly questioned the war and blamed it for the Republicans' midterm rout, he voiced support for Hegseth on Tuesday. "This isn't about Iran, this is about the fact that Pete took on the bureaucracy at the Pentagon," Vance wrote on social media. Before the vote, House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries said on Monday: "Pete Hegseth has abused his power, undermined America's national security, and he's the architect of the reckless and costly failed war of choice in Iran." Hegseth has repeatedly defended the conflict, calling Trump courageous and saying Iran's military has been left in ruins. He also said his orders to US forces were lawful, despite Massie's accusations of "high crimes and misdemeanours". "History will judge the Iran war quite differently than the conventional wisdom right now," Hegseth said on Tuesday at his first Pentagon briefing in six months. Jeffries said he would talk to members about whether to mount a new impeachment effort in the next Congress. "We'll have that conversation at the appropriate time," he said. A Democratic-led push to impeach Hegseth could be far more intense, with lawmakers calling in top brass to testify, including generals and admirals fired by Hegseth who have remained silent so far. Hegseth, who has railed against diversity efforts at the Pentagon, fired the chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, who is Black, and the Navy's top admiral, a woman, among others. In such an effort, Democrats could also raise other issues of concern to voters including Pentagon policy toward Ukraine and the US military's strikes on suspected drug trafficking boats in Caribbean and Pacific waters. Some Republicans say Hegseth's strained relations with Congress are becoming a political liability as the Trump administration seeks a huge increase in the military's budget to US$1.5 trillion from US$950 billion. Massie said he was disappointed by the vote, comparing Republicans to passengers content to go down with the Titanic. "They know it's a sinking ship but committed to stay on board," he said.

Source: Reuters/fh/ec

item.title: Israel's parliament sworn in as Eisenkot tries to forge a government
item.description: Israeli President Isaac Herzog urged lawmakers to "do everything to avoid another election”.
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:

Israel's parliament sworn in as Eisenkot tries to forge a government

Israeli President Isaac Herzog urged lawmakers to "do everything to avoid another election”.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, and lawmaker Gadi Eisenkot, pose for a group photo after the swearing-in ceremony for Israeli lawmakers at the Knesset, Israel's parliament, in Jerusalem, on Nov 10, 2026. (Photo: AP/Ohad Zwigenberg)

11 Nov 2026 04:48AM (Updated: 11 Nov 2026 07:15AM)

FAST

JERUSALEM: Israel 's parliament was sworn in on Tuesday (Nov 10) without a new government , after a deadlocked general election stripped Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of his parliamentary majority but left his main rivals with no clear path to power. Lawmakers elected in the Oct 27 vote took their oaths of office as Gadi Eisenkot , a former general, sought to forge a coalition after Israel 's president tasked him on Sunday with forming a government . Eisenkot and his allies also lack a majority and he has yet to strike deals with parties that could bring him to power. If both Eisenkot and Netanyahu fail to form coalitions, another election could follow. Presiding over the swearing-in ceremony, President Isaac Herzog told lawmakers: "You must do everything to avoid a repeat election."

"Reach out a hand for compromise, even between rivals ... Look upon one another with generosity. There is much work to be done here, and it requires the ability and experience found in every part of this House."

PARLIAMENT COULD TRY TO SET UP OCT 7 INQUIRY Netanyahu remains caretaker prime minister until a new candidate manages to form a coalition. His right-wing Likud party's alliance with far-right and ultra-Orthodox parties outperformed election expectations but still lost its majority, now holding 53 of the Knesset's 120 seats. Eisenkot's centre-right Yashar party and patchwork partner factions hold just 48 seats. But they have potential allies in Israel 's Arab-led parties, which hold 19 seats and are aligned with Eisenkot in their vehement opposition to Netanyahu . This means that the newly sworn-in parliament could still deliver on some of Eisenkot's campaign promises, such as potentially setting up a commission of inquiry into the Oct 7, 2023 Hamas attacks, something backed by the Arab parties but largely opposed by Netanyahu . It also could allow Eisenkot to replace the current Knesset speaker, a Likud member. Herzog told Knesset members that parliament was "duty bound to leave no stone unturned" in investigating and understanding the "catastrophe" of Oct 7, while Israel continues to face threats from Iran and its proxies. Eisenkot initially has until Dec 6 to form a government but he can seek a two-week extension to Dec 20. He has acknowledged his path to power is "extraordinarily complex". His options include trying to form a minority government with Arab party support, bringing ultra-Orthodox parties into his camp despite years of mutual hostility, or forging a unity government with Netanyahu . All three paths face formidable obstacles. Ultra-Orthodox parties have so far said they would not join an Eisenkot-led government .

Related:

How Israel's new parliament can make Netanyahu's life difficult

Netanyahu rival Eisenkot seeks 'wide' government but path to power uncertain

Israel faces new era of sinking US support after election

For his part, Netanyahu has cast doubt on the election results by baselessly alleging voter fraud by Arabs, who make up a fifth of the population. Election officials have said they are probing potential misconduct, but that they have seen no evidence of fraud that could have influenced the vote's outcome. Speaking after parliament was sworn in, Netanyahu called for a unity government , warning that Iran was seeking to revive its nuclear programme and that Israel could come under growing international pressure to accept a nuclear-armed Iran. "Only such a (unity) government will be capable of confronting challenges of this magnitude," he said. If Eisenkot fails to form a government , Herzog would likely ask Netanyahu to try to build a coalition. If he also fails, another candidate would get a chance before Israel would be forced into another election. Moments after the official opening of parliament, Eisenkot and his allies submitted a series of bills, including legislation to establish a state commission of inquiry into the Oct 7 attacks and to impose term limits on the prime minister. They also proposed repealing a controversial judicial overhaul and other laws enacted under Netanyahu 's government over the past four years. Among those sworn in on Tuesday was Elisha Madan, a military reservist who lost both legs fighting in Gaza. He received a standing ovation from lawmakers as he rose on his prosthetic legs to take the oath of office.

Source: Reuters/fs

News / Stock Story / Plug Power, JELD-WEN, Trex, GE Vernova, and Hertz shares are falling, what you need to know

Plug Power, JELD-WEN, Trex, GE Vernova, and Hertz shares are falling, what you need to know 2 min read

PLUG JELD TREX GEV

What happened? A number of stocks fell in the afternoon session after the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported that the Consumer Price Index increased 0.4 percent in October 2026, highlighting persistent price pressures across the economy. The latest inflation figures showed that underlying inflation remains resilient, with the core Consumer Price Index—which excludes volatile food and energy costs—advancing 0.3 percent over the month. Sticky inflation complicates corporate operating environments by elevating input costs and weakening consumer spending power. When consumer price gauges climb faster than expected, market participants often reassess future earnings expectations, particularly for high-growth technology firms whose future cash flows are heavily sensitive to macroeconomic headwinds. Sector-wide sentiment turned cautious as investors factored in the potential durability of elevated cost structures across operations. The stock market overreacts to news, and big price drops can present good opportunities to buy high-quality stocks. Among others, the following stocks were impacted: Renewable energy company Plug Power PLUG fell 8.7%. Is now the time to buy Plug Power? Access our full analysis report here, it’s free. Home construction materials company JELD-WEN JELD fell 12.8%. Is now the time to buy JELD-WEN? Access our full analysis report here, it’s free. Home construction materials company Trex TREX fell 7.1%. Is now the time to buy Trex? Access our full analysis report here, it’s free. Electrical systems company GE Vernova GEV fell 7.2%. Is now the time to buy GE Vernova? Access our full analysis report here, it’s free. Ground transportation company Hertz HTZ fell 4.6%. Is now the time to buy Hertz? Access our full analysis report here, it’s free. Zooming in on JELD-WEN (JELD) JELD-WEN’s shares are extremely volatile and have had 98 moves greater than 5% over the last year. But moves this big are rare even for JELD-WEN and indicate this news significantly impacted the market’s perception of the business. The previous big move we wrote about was about 24 hours ago when the stock gained 12.1% on the news that falling crude oil prices fueled a broad market rebound and eased cost concerns surrounding artificial intelligence data center construction. CNBC reported that the major indexes rallied as oil prices dropped. In the session, Brent was down about 4% to around $94 a barrel and West Texas Intermediate was down about 3% to around $87. United States equities rallied to claw back losses from the prior week as retreating crude benchmarks alleviated inflationary headwinds across major industries. Lower energy prices are particularly advantageous for energy-intensive sectors, offering timely relief to developers scaling artificial intelligence facilities. Construction of hyperscale data centers requires substantial capital and power resources, making sustained high energy costs a threat to projected operating margins. As fuel costs swung lower, concerns regarding buildout budgets diminished, driving broad-based investor optimism across the technology and infrastructure ecosystem. JELD-WEN is down 58.3% since the beginning of the year, and at $1.04 per share, it is trading 67.5% below its 52-week high of $3.18 from January 2026. Investors who bought $1,000 worth of JELD-WEN’s shares 5 years ago would now be looking at only $39.22. ONE MORE THING: The $21 AI Application Stock Wall Street Forgot. item.title: Gold price falls nearly 3% as CPI tops forecasts, lifting dollar and yields
item.description: Gold prices fell nearly 3% on Tuesday after hotter-than-expected US inflation data lifted the dollar and Treasury yields while reinforcing expectations of a
item.dc:creator: Mining.com
item.content:encoded: Gold prices fell nearly 3% on Tuesday after hotter-than-expected US inflation data lifted the dollar and Treasury yields while reinforcing expectations of a bigger interest rate hike from the Federal Reserve this year. Spot gold XAU= was down 2.8% at $4,021.36 per ounce by 11:33 a.m. ET (1635 GMT). US gold futures GCcv1 for December delivery fell 1.9% to $4,036.00 per ounce. “I think it’s a bit of a short-term negative for gold because the inflation numbers were running a little higher than expected,” said Edward Meir, an analyst at Marex. The US Consumer Price Index rose 0.4% last month after advancing 0.6% in September, the Labor Department’s Bureau of Labor Statistics said. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast a 0.3% month-on-month rise. Bets on a 50-basis-point Fed rate hike in December started to build after the inflation print and comments by Fed governor Christopher Waller, who said he would support more aggressive action in the event of a too-hot Consumer Price Index report. The probability of a 25 bp hike is fully priced in, while the possibility of a 50 bp hike rose to 10.5% from 0% before the data, according to CME’s FedWatch Tool. The US dollar .DXY rose against a basket of other major currencies, and Treasury yields climbed. A stronger dollar makes gold more expensive for overseas buyers, while higher Treasury yields increase the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding bullion. “(Gold) continues to trade above the critical $4,000/oz mark,” Standard Chartered said in a note, adding “crude oil, inflation risks and equity markets continue to set the tone of trading for gold with a focus on rate hike expectations for the December Fed meeting.” Meanwhile, the Monetary Authority of Singapore said it would launch a vaulting service to hold bullion for foreign central banks and lower taxes on some companies in the gold market as it competes for a bigger slice of the precious metals trade. Spot silver XAG= fell 3.9% to $51.32 per ounce and palladium XPD= was down 2.0% at $1,021.22. (Reporting by Vedika Thorat and Anjana Anil in Bengaluru; Editing by Kirsten Donovan and Jonathan Ananda)

item.title: US CPI Exceeds Expectations Again, Waller's Warning Comes True! Wall Street Focuses on Whether December Rate Hike Will Be 25 or 50 Basis Points; "New Fed News Agency": Stop-and-Go Strategy Faces Test
item.description: The "New Federal Reserve Newsletter" pointed out that before the release of the CPI, Waller suggested the possibility of a 50-basis-point rate hike in December, and so far, no other Fed officials have publicly responded. In addition to a single 50-basis-point hike, the Fed may also choose to signal consecutive rate hikes in December and January. Wall Street generally believes that inflationary pressures remain stubborn, further strengthening the case for a rate hike in December, though a 50-basis-point increase is not a consensus. The market is concerned about whether the Fed will extend the tightening cycle.
item.dc:creator: 华尔街见闻
item.content:encoded: US inflation in October once again exceeded expectations, further raising market expectations for a Federal Reserve rate hike in December, with the possibility of a larger rate increase now being discussed. The US Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) announced on Tuesday, November 10, that the October CPI rose 0.4% month-on-month, lower than the 0.6% increase in September but higher than economists’ forecasts of 0.3%. The core CPI rose 0.3% month-on-month, matching September’s increase and exceeding the market’s expectation of 0.2%. This marks the third consecutive month where overall CPI rose more than Wall Street predicted, and core CPI has also climbed 0.3% month-on-month for three straight months. Due to the failure to collect CPI data during the US federal government shutdown in October 2025, the BLS was unable to provide a year-on-year figure for October CPI. This report precisely meets the policy threshold previously outlined by Federal Reserve Governor Waller. Just hours before the CPI was published, Waller stated that if the core CPI for October increased by 0.3% or more month-on-month, he might support a 50 basis point rate hike at the Fed’s monetary policy meeting in December. With this criterion now met, the market’s bets on a 50 basis point rate hike in December have gained momentum. Nick Timiraos, a journalist nicknamed the “New Fed Whisperer,” pointed out that this inflation report is testing the Fed’s previous strategy of “spacing out rate hikes,” using staggered moves to leave room to monitor economic data. The choices facing policymakers are not only between a 25 or 50 basis point hike in December, but also whether to adjust the pace of subsequent actions, or even to signal back-to-back rate hikes in December and January of next year. Wall Street’s reaction is showing a common assessment: inflationary pressures remain stubborn, providing more justification for a December rate hike, though opinions differ on the size of the increase. Some believe that three consecutive months of core CPI climbing 0.3% makes it difficult for the Fed to ignore the inflation rebound; others feel that a 50-basis-point hike may be too aggressive and that 25 basis points is still the more realistic option. The market’s real concern is not just the decision at the next meeting but also whether the Fed may extend the tightening cycle as a result. “New Fed Whisperer”: Core prices strengthen across the board, Fed could signal back-to-back hikes In his analysis in The Wall Street Journal, Timiraos noted that the strong showing of October inflation is testing the Fed’s strategy of spreading out rate hikes across different meetings to allow time to observe economic data. He noted that Waller has raised the possibility that if the third month’s inflation data remains hot, a 50-basis-point rate hike in December could be on the table. However, no other Fed officials have publicly echoed this position as of yet. The Fed could also choose another way to address inflationary pressures: instead of a one-off 50-basis-point increase at a single meeting, it could signal consecutive rate hikes in December and January. According to Timiraos, this could be one way to adjust the policy pace. The last time the Fed raised rates by more than 25 basis points at once was back in 2022. On social media, Timiraos further broke down the details of core inflation, pointing out that core prices “strengthened broadly” in October. Specifically, core goods prices rose at a 1% annualized pace over the past six months, compared with just 0.1% in the previous period through June; core services prices excluding shelter rose 0.4% in October, about 4.9% annualized, while three- and six-month annualized increases stood at 5.5% and 3.2% respectively. He also pointed out that the unrounded month-on-month increase in core CPI for October was 0.296%, marking the third straight month at about 0.3%. The three-month annualized rate for core CPI climbed to 3.75%, compared with only 1.6% in July. This data shows that inflationary pressures are not just driven by overall energy price increases—core goods and services prices are also consistently strengthening. For the Fed, this makes it harder to treat inflation as a short-term shock and simply wait for price pressures to subside on their own. Waller raises 50-basis-point option, market begins to reassess policy strength Just hours before the CPI was released, Waller gave a hawkish speech while attending an event in London. He said the US economy was experiencing strong growth and a stable labor market, but inflation remained too high, requiring the Fed to “tighten policy sooner rather than later.” Waller had previously supported the Fed’s decision to keep rates unchanged at the last meeting, arguing that previous policy communications had already led financial markets to price in some degree of tightening. He believes policy adjustments do not have to be implemented in consecutive meetings, but prior guidance on rate hikes must eventually be delivered on, otherwise markets may lower expectations for further tightening, causing financial conditions to ease prematurely. Regarding the December meeting, Waller had already indicated before the CPI was published that if the October core CPI once again rose by around 0.3% month-on-month (as in the previous two months) or even higher, more forceful policy action might be needed. He explicitly raised the possibility of a 50-basis-point hike, and warned that if inflation remained high and price pressures broadened, raising rates by only 25 basis points could hurt the Fed’s credibility in fighting inflation. Ultimately, the October core CPI met this threshold. According to Reuters, after the data was announced, market expectations for a 25-basis-point rate hike in December were almost certain, and bets on a 50-basis-point hike rose to about 15% at one point. The two-year US Treasury yield surged, recording its largest single-day rise since early April 2025. However, Timiraos also cautioned that no other Fed official has publicly echoed Waller’s 50-basis-point position so far. Thus, the market’s discussion of a larger rate hike does not necessarily mean consensus within the Fed. Wall Street divided: Inflation pressures cannot be ignored, but 50 basis points is not a consensus After the inflation data was released, several Wall Street figures said the reasons for a December Fed rate hike had increased, but assessments of the scale and the persistence of inflation pressures varied. Omair Sharif, President of Inflation Insights, commented that the latest report “offers little to ease market concerns about persistent inflation risks” and does not dispel the Fed’s reasons for further hikes. He also estimated that the October core PCE price index might climb by 0.34%, representing an annualized increase of over 4%, higher than the previous month. While the Fed’s 2% policy target is based on headline PCE inflation, core PCE better reflects the underlying inflation trend. If this estimate is confirmed by subsequent data, it would further justify Fed tightening. James McCann, Senior Economist at Edward Jones, described this as another “disappointing inflation report,” reflecting that underlying price pressures may be building again. With US economic growth and the labor market both clearly accelerating this year, and core inflation showing signs of reacceleration, the Fed faces even greater policy pressure. McCann pointed out that the real worry is whether inflation is settling at a higher level. He argued the report at least solidifies the rationale for a 25-basis-point hike in December, while the bigger debate has become whether the Fed needs a 50-basis-point hike and more aggressive action. Peter Cardillo, Chief Market Economist at Spartan Capital Securities, also believes a December rate hike is virtually certain, with the suspense lying in whether it will be 25 or 50 basis points. He commented that Waller has effectively paved the way for a half-point hike, and the latest data shows inflation remains an issue. However, Cardillo also cautioned that circumstances could still change over the next 30 to 40 days. Should oil prices retreat and pass through to consumer prices, inflationary pressures may ease; but if oil rebounds, the inflation outlook could deteriorate again. Chris Zaccarelli, Chief Investment Officer at Northlight Asset Management, believes inflation above an ideal level further increases the likelihood of a December Fed hike. Still, despite market calls for a 50-basis-point hike, he expects the Fed will only lift rates by 25 basis points next month. Joe Saluzzi, Co-Head of Themis Trading, likewise noted that persistently high core inflation shows that price pressures have “stickiness” and that a 25-basis-point hike remains realistic, while 50 basis points may be too aggressive. He also warned that prolonged high rates and inflation will continue to pressure borrowing-dependent businesses, affecting profits and stock valuations. Skyler Weinand, Chief Investment Officer at Regan Capital, stated that the latest CPI paves the way for another Fed rate hike in December—the central bank cannot ignore the clear rebound in inflation data. He also pointed out that the latest jobs report showed robust employment gains in October as well as upward revisions to previous months’ data, providing the Fed with more room for further hikes. Labor market remains resilient, tightening policies may persist longer Besides inflation itself, the continued resilience of the US labor market also provides the Fed more leeway to prioritize combating inflation in its policy decisions. In his speech on Tuesday, Waller noted that US unemployment fell to 4.1% in October, with 165,000 new jobs added that month and a combined upward revision of 85,000 jobs over the prior two months. Although the average monthly jobs gains over the past six and twelve months is about 80,000, the overall labor market remains in a broadly balanced state, with no significant deterioration. This means the Fed, faced with persistently high inflation, need not worry about the impact of rate hikes on jobs as much as it would if the labor market were visibly weakening. Brian Jacobsen, Chief Economic Strategist at Annex Wealth Management, pointed out from a price transmission angle that three consecutive months of core CPI rising 0.3% month-on-month shows that the issue isn’t just high headline CPI, but that energy shocks may have begun to seep into core inflation. He also mentioned that Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee previously discussed how AI demand could be a new source of inflationary pressure for the Fed. As AI investment and infrastructure expansion rise, economic activity may crowd out resources in other areas and push up prices for some services. Jacobsen suggests the Fed may increasingly focus on the resource squeeze from AI demand and rising wage costs for skilled trades like plumbers and electricians. Jeff Schulze, Chief Investment Strategist at Franklin Templeton Institute, warned that the latest inflation data will serve as a headwind for risk assets. Investors are beginning to price in a 50-basis-point December hike and more afterward; rising short-term yields and a stronger US dollar could both suppress equity valuations. Karen Manna, Fixed Income Investment Strategist at Federated Hermes, also said the report strengthens the rationale for another Fed rate hike and further demands policymakers maintain vigilance. The real concern for investors is that if inflation remains high, the Fed may have to keep monetary policy restrictive for an extended period, well into 2027. Overall, the October CPI brings a December rate hike closer to market consensus, but the policy options facing the Fed are no longer just whether to raise rates. Waller’s 50-basis-point option, Timiraos’ comments on rate-hike spacing, and whether other officials will support speeding up the pace of tightening—all will be key market focuses going forward.
